findings.text: _mapped_region_count is monkeypatched in every test that exercises the trigger (tests/test_jax_config.py:128 and :140), so the one function the containment depends on is never run against a real /proc/self/maps; a regression in it (a wrong path, counting bytes instead of lines, or returning 0 on any OSError as it already does) leaves tests/test_jax_config.py fully green while release_compilation_caches_when_mapped silently never fires.

the autouse fixture is the containment itself and nothing in the fast lane asserts it is registered or applied, so deleting it reddens no test short of the multi-hour arm; an assertion that the fixture name is in a case's fixturenames would make that regression visible in the fast default selection.

the expected before/after counts come from the test's own stub iterator (counts = iter((3, 0)) at :109), so the release assertion pins the re-read wiring rather than a measured reduction: it reddens if the code stops calling _live_executable_count after the clear, but it holds whatever jax.clear_caches actually does, and reverting the release's effect leaves it true.
